triggers: a kernel on NVIDIA Blackwell GeForce/workstation (RTX PRO 5000 / SM120) risks the '18. Shared fp32 state-MMA can remove FFMA but still lose' trap

payload.goal: Avoid a known trap on NVIDIA Blackwell GeForce/workstation (RTX PRO 5000 / SM120): 18. Shared fp32 state-MMA can remove FFMA but still lose

problem.statement: GDN Chunk Forward Pitfalls (CuTeDSL, SM120) -- 18. Shared fp32 state-MMA can remove FFMA but still lose

payload.attempted: Move the recurrent state into fp32 shared memory and use HMMA-like state updates to remove scalar FFMA work.
payload.lesson: Keep the recurrent state register-resident. Use shared memory only as a bf16 MMA operand bridge, and make those bridges R2S/LDSM-friendly.

established_fact.mechanism: Persisting fp32 state in shared memory adds large shared stores/loads and extra barriers. The old scalar compute wall disappears, but it is replaced by a shared-memory dependency wall.

payload.observed: The probe was correct, and SASS did remove the old FFMA/SHF/PRMT wall, but performance regressed to about `1.26 ms` or worse. Registers and shared-memory traffic collapsed occupancy and scheduler eligibility.
payload.root_cause: Persisting fp32 state in shared memory adds large shared stores/loads and extra barriers. The old scalar compute wall disappears, but it is replaced by a shared-memory dependency wall.
